hypothesis: Adding a pre_answer_emit REACTIVE_GUARD that synthesises a best-guess FINAL ANSWER via ctx.chat() from gathered tool evidence (when ctx.answer is empty) lifts train-30 accuracy from 16/30 (0.533) to ~19-22/30 (0.633-0.733) by recovering a non-trivial fraction of the 13 tasks that currently exit with empty answer after run.exhausted_iterations.
changes: ADD a new component file agent/components/component_iter1_exhaustion_recovery.py. The component subscribes to pre_answer_emit; its matcher fires iff ctx.answer is empty/None. The handler reads ctx.log.path (the EventLog's flushed JSONL trace) to reconstruct (question, last <=12 tool_call/result pairs, last assistant draft), each tool result truncated to 1500 chars, then issues a single ctx.chat() call (locked SUT model, max_tokens=4096, temperature=0.0) with a recovery system prompt that mirrors the GAIA FINAL-ANSWER format. The returned content is run through agent.base._extract_final_answer; a non-empty extracted answer is REWRITE'd back into ctx.answer. All failure paths (missing log, unreadable trace, chat exception, empty recovery, no extractable answer) fall through to Decision.allow() so the original empty answer is preserved.

trust.evidence_anchor: agent.base._extract_final_answer returns '' iff the final LLM turn carries no content (direct consequence of run.exhausted_iterations); ctx.log.path is a flushed-per-emit JSONL trace (agent/events.py::EventLog) with a published schema (run.started/tool.called/tool.responded/llm.responded); the GAIA scorer awards 0 to '' by construction. The synthesis mechanism (re-prompt the locked SUT with (question, gathered tool results) and extract a FINAL ANSWER line) is a general algorithm independent of any task content.
trust.rollback_when: train-30 accuracy decreases vs the iter0 frontier — i.e. the synthesis somehow overrides a correct ctx.answer (matcher should make this impossible) or the recovery model produces mis-formatted output causing scorer false-negatives on previously-passing tasks.
trust.out_of_evidence_probe: Case A: a task where the FC loop emits 'FINAL ANSWER: 42' cleanly — ctx.answer='42', matcher returns False, handler never fires, answer unchanged. Case B: a task where ctx.answer is empty AND the agent made zero tool calls (early refusal) — handler still runs but evidence is '(no tool calls were made)' so the locked model is forced to attempt cold from the question; worst case still scores 0, no regression.
trust.fallback: Matcher returns False when ctx.answer is non-empty. Handler returns Decision.allow() on: missing log.path, unreadable trace file, ctx.chat() exception, empty recovery content, or no extractable FINAL ANSWER.

hypothesis: Adding a MECHANISM_LAYER on post_llm_response that queues an escalating turn-budget warning (delivered as a system note on the next turn) when current_iter is within 3 of MAX_ITERATIONS AND finish_reason is 'tool_calls' lifts train-30 accuracy from 18/30 (0.600) to roughly 20-22/30 (0.667-0.733) by converting a fraction of the 10 train-30 failures that exited with raw_answer='' after run.exhausted_iterations into runs where the agent voluntarily emits a FINAL ANSWER before hard-stop.
changes: ADD a new component file agent/components/component_iter2_turn_budget_warner.py. It subscribes to post_llm_response; the matcher fires iff ctx.current_iter is in [MAX_ITERATIONS-_WARN_REMAINING, MAX_ITERATIONS) (i.e., turns 12, 13, 14) AND ctx.shared['finish_reason']=='tool_calls' (the LLM is still requesting tools, has not committed to an answer). The handler returns Decision.inject_context(...) with a system warning naming the exact number of turns remaining and asking the agent to commit to a FINAL ANSWER now in the GAIA answer format. The warning lands as a system note on the next turn via the standard ctx.shared['post_llm_inject'] queue. No rewrite, no block.

hypothesis: Adding a MECHANISM_LAYER on post_llm_response that fires ONCE per task — strictly at iter MAX_ITERATIONS-1 (=14) AND only when finish_reason=='tool_calls' — and injects a system note that lands at iter 15's pre-LLM phase will lift train-30 accuracy from 18/30 (0.600) to roughly 20-22/30 (0.667-0.733). The notice tells the agent that iter 15 is its FINAL turn and asks it to commit a FINAL ANSWER line. On the iter1-frontier failures, 8 of 11 tasks exit with raw_answer='' after run.exhausted_iterations; on those, the LLM at iter 15 has full reasoning_content and tool-message context, while exhaustion_answer_recovery only sees a truncated trace summary — so a successfully-prompted iter-15 commit should beat recovery's blind guess in answer quality.
changes: ADD a new component file agent/components/component_iter3_final_turn_commit_notice.py exporting COMPONENT (MECHANISM_LAYER, listens='post_llm_response'). The matcher fires iff ctx.current_iter == MAX_ITERATIONS-1 (=14) AND ctx.shared['finish_reason']=='tool_calls' AND ctx.state['fired'] is not already True. The handler sets ctx.state['fired']=True and returns Decision.inject_context(notice_text). The notice tells the agent that iter 15 is the FINAL turn (no more tool calls possible after) and asks it to end its next response with 'FINAL ANSWER: <value>'. Per dispatcher routing for non-setup, non-tool events, the inject_context payload is appended to ctx.shared['post_llm_inject'] and drained by the FC loop at the top of iter 15's pre-LLM phase, landing as a fresh system message in iter 15's chat() call. Strictly narrower than iter2's rejected turn_budget_warner: ONE fire per task (at iter 14, not iters 12+13+14) and only on the exhaustion failure path (finish_reason='tool_calls'). hypothesis: Replacing length_recovery_guard with a version that reads the agent's prior conversation history from ctx.log.path (the most recent llm.requested.messages payload) and re-prompts the locked SUT with that full history plus a 'commit FINAL ANSWER now' system override will lift train-30 accuracy from 21/30 (0.700) to roughly 22-23/30 (0.733-0.767). Direct evidence is task 9b54f9d9 in the iter3 train-30 trace: agent successfully read the input zip, ran a python_exec on the contents, then hit finish_reason='length' mid-reasoning on iter 3; the prior length_recovery_guard re-asked the original prompt cold and produced 'CATEGORIES\nCURRY' (ground truth: 'Soups and Stews'). Structurally the prior recovery loses all conversation context by construction, so the fix applies to any task that hits length truncation after non-trivial tool use, not only to 9b54f9d9.

hypothesis: Adding a REACTIVE_GUARD on `on_tool_error` that injects a pattern-aware structural pivot hint (HTTP 4xx vs 5xx vs invalid-URL-scheme vs generic) INTO ctx.current_tool_result on the 2nd+ tool error per task will lift train-30 accuracy from 22/30 (0.7333 — iter4 frontier acc on the latest re-score) towards ~24-26/30 (0.80-0.867) by curbing the consecutive-4xx URL-variant-guessing pattern that bleeds turns on tasks like 48eb8242 (6 url_fetch 404s in a row on the same host), 5f982798 (4 errors), 853c8244 (4 errors), and 16d825ff (2 errors).
changes: ADD a new component file agent/components/component_iter6_tool_error_pivot_hint.py exporting COMPONENT (REACTIVE_GUARD, listens='on_tool_error'). The matcher returns True at every fire (the runtime already gates the event on tool result.startswith('ERROR')). The handler increments a per-task per-component counter on ctx.state['err_count']; suppresses on the FIRST error (single transient errors recover on their own — see ad37a656 / 0ff53813 / 114d5fd0 / 544b7f0c which all scored 1 with exactly one success=false in iter5); on the 2nd+ error, classifies the error string against (tool_name, error-pattern) into one of four buckets — HTTP 4xx, HTTP 5xx, malformed URL scheme, or generic — and returns Decision.inject_context(hint). Per the dispatcher, INJECT_CONTEXT @ on_tool_error CONCATENATES the hint INTO ctx.current_tool_result (agent/component_runtime/base.py L190-192), so the LLM sees the original 'ERROR HTTP ...' line plus the hint as part of the same tool-response message on the next turn. The hook never modifies ctx.current_tool_success, never blocks, never rewrites. Workflow patch: add 'tool_error_pivot_hint' as a new node in meta_harness/workflows/gaia_main.yaml after final_turn_commit_notice.

trust.evidence_anchor: Three stable contracts outside the evidence trace: (1) the component runtime synthesises on_tool_error iff tool result.startswith('ERROR') (agent/component_runtime/base.py L434 + L441-444); (2) HTTP status code semantics per RFC 9110 §15.5 (4xx = permanent client-side error, retrying same URL is futile) and §15.6 (5xx = server error, possibly transient) — a protocol-level fact independent of any task content; (3) the dispatcher's INJECT_CONTEXT @ on_tool_error placement (agent/component_runtime/base.py::_apply_decision L190-192 concatenates the payload INTO ctx.current_tool_result), so the hint becomes part of the tool-response message the LLM sees on the next turn; it never overwrites the original error string. The hint text is a general control-loop heuristic ('on permanent failure, pivot strategy rather than retry') keyed on the tool's documented error format and HTTP status code class — not on any task-specific evidence.
trust.rollback_when: train-30 accuracy decreases below the iter5 frontier score (24/30) — i.e., the hint causes the LLM to abandon a viable retry path it would have completed on its own, or the additional tool-message text crowds the context enough to surface more length truncations downstream.
trust.out_of_evidence_probe: Case A: a task with zero tool errors — on_tool_error never fires, ctx.state.err_count stays 0, hint never injected, no behavioural change. Case B: a task with exactly one transient tool error that the agent self-recovers from (e.g. ad37a656 in the iter5 trace set, score 1) — handler increments err_count to 1, below threshold, returns allow(); no hint, no regression. Case C: a tool error on a tool not enumerated in _classify (future tool registration) — falls through to the generic 'tool returned an error' hint; safe additive text. Case D: ctx.current_tool_result is empty or None at on_tool_error (would imply a runtime bug — the event is synthesised only when the result starts with 'ERROR') — handler short-circuits to allow().
trust.fallback: Matcher always returns True (event already gated by the runtime). Handler returns Decision.allow() on: empty/null ctx.current_tool_result, fewer than _MIN_ERRORS_BEFORE_HINT errors so far in this task, or _classify returning an empty string. A missed-fire path produces no rewrite and no block, leaving ctx.current_tool_result untouched. The hint, when injected, is APPENDED to the existing error text — the original error string is never lost.

hypothesis: Raising exhaustion_answer_recovery's per-call output ceiling from 4096 to 16384 tokens will lift train-30 accuracy from 17/30 (iter6 single-run baseline; iter6 frontier 24/30) to roughly 18-20/30, recovering ~1 of the 4 train-30 failures that currently exhaust at iter 15 with raw_answer='' AND whose recovery returns Decision.allow rather than a confidently-wrong rewrite (direct evidence: e142056d-56ab-4352-b091-b56054bd1359, the only iter6 exhaustion_answer_recovery fire that resolved as `allow` per .component-state/iter6/fired.jsonl line 77). With the locked SUT in deepseek thinking mode (reasoning_content emitted separately, max_tokens bounding the TOTAL reasoning+content output per OpenAI spec), the recovery model on hard reasoning tasks spends its 4096-token budget inside reasoning_content and emits empty content — so content.strip() is empty and the handler falls through to allow(), preserving the empty answer the GAIA scorer marks 0. A 16384-token ceiling gives the recovery model enough headroom to finish thinking AND emit a single FINAL ANSWER line. max_tokens is a CEILING (per Chat Completions spec) so this never alters behaviour on the 5 train-30 tasks where iter1's exhaustion_answer_recovery already produces a correct synthesis.
changes: REPLACE the existing exhaustion_answer_recovery component (agent/components/component_iter1_exhaustion_recovery.py; .bak_iter7 written first per the replace protocol). The ONLY behavioural change is the module-level constant `_RECOVERY_MAX_TOKENS` going from 4096 to 16384, passed unchanged into ctx.chat(max_tokens=...). All failure paths (missing log, unreadable trace, no llm.requested events, chat exception, empty recovery, no extractable FINAL ANSWER) still fall through to Decision.allow(), preserving the iter0 baseline behaviour as a strict floor. Docstring and Trust.evidence_anchor / Trust.rollback_when / Trust.out_of_evidence_probe / Trust.fallback are updated to document the new ceiling and reference the OpenAI Chat Completions API spec on max_tokens as a stable contract. Workflow patch op is `replace` (no node name change).

hypothesis: Adding a MECHANISM_LAYER on pre_answer_emit that strips leaked Markdown emphasis wrappers (**, __, ~~, `) from ctx.answer will lift train-30 single-run accuracy from 18/30 (iter7) toward 19-20/30 by curing variance failures of the form `**FINAL ANSWER: <x>**` — where the published `_extract_final_answer` regex `r"FINAL ANSWER:\s*(.+?)\s*$"` captures the trailing `**` into the extracted answer because the literal `FINAL ANSWER:` anchor sits AFTER the opening `**`. Direct evidence: iter7 task 50ec8903 emitted `green, white**` (GT `green, white`, scored 0); iter2 task 4d0aa727 emitted `1 in 3**` (GT `1 in 3`, scored 0). Both tasks score 1.0 in the frontier under other runs, so this is a variance-stabilization fix, not a hard-task fix.
changes: ADD a new component file agent/components/component_iter8_answer_markdown_strip.py exporting COMPONENT (MECHANISM_LAYER, listens='pre_answer_emit', priority=130 so it fires AFTER exhaustion_answer_recovery at the same event). Matcher: ctx.answer is non-empty AND `_strip_wrappers(answer) != answer`. Handler: returns Decision.rewrite(cleaned). Stripping logic iteratively applies (a) symmetric multi-char or backtick wrappers (`**…**`, `__…__`, `~~…~~`, `` `…` ``) when both ends agree AND len > 2*|w|, then (b) asymmetric trailing multi-char wrappers (`**`, `__`, `~~`) when the same wrapper is NOT also present inside the remaining span, then (c) symmetric asymmetric leading multi-char wrappers under the same constraint. Single-char `*` / `_` are never asymmetric-stripped (preserves legitimate math / footnote markers).
